Why is this needed if FutureSkills, Skill India and IndiaAI exist?
They built access at scale (34L FSP registrants, 85.27L YUVA). Public records stop at certificates; we add the outcome layer, not another platform.
What exactly is missing?
Verified competence, workplace evidence and outcome tracking — e.g., no placement/competency field in FSP's public release; only 1,480 AI-role NAPS-2 apprentices FY23–26.
Why should government build this rather than industry?
Standards, interoperability, portability and equity are public goods; firms under-invest in skills workers can take elsewhere.
Why would employers participate?
Pre-verified talent, co-funded projects via challenge fund, input into competency standards.
Why would providers change behaviour?
65% of each fee is paid only after competency, project and work evidence.
How does this reach Tier-3 and rural India?
Hubs on PM-SETU ITIs, NIELIT (56 centres, 9,000+ partners) and IndiaAI labs; CSC-assisted, voice/vernacular via BHASHINI; offline modules.
How does it help mid-career workers?
₹15–25k credit, 8–12-week employer-validated L2 track, AI Transition Exchange for internal moves. Benchmark: Singapore's S$4,000 at 40+.
How do we prevent certificate inflation?
Credits and payments tied to independent assessment; accreditation; integrity audits.
How do we prove actual competency?
Independent NCVET-recognised assessors + applied project + employer validation + periodic reassessment.
How does the Passport differ from existing credentials?
It records verified level, projects, employer validation and refresh history on one national scale, riding APAAR/ABC/DigiLocker — not a new ID.
How does the programme avoid duplication?
National convergence dashboard across MeitY/MSDE/MoE schemes; Council owns taxonomy.
What if employers don't provide apprenticeships?
Challenge fund, MSME problem statements at hubs, public departments as employer-of-first-resort.
What if the ₹290 Cr pilot fails?
Gates stop or redesign it; loss is capped; India still gains its first outcome baseline.
Why ₹290 Cr?
Bottom-up: ≈10,000 apprentices × ₹70k; ≈50,000 credits × ₹5k; ≈35 hubs; ≈1.5L assessments; 5% contingency; ≈3.4% evaluation (see Budget_Model).
Why ₹6,500 Cr?
Implies ≈₹7,000 per role-ready learner and ≈₹2 lakh per advanced practitioner; central share ≈₹800 Cr/yr ≈ 8% of MSDE FY27 allocation; much is convergence of existing spend.
What is the economic return?
We don't claim one. Break-even: ≈₹48,000 of gain per verified convert; measured in conservative/base/upside cases.
How is ROI measured?
(Benefit − Cost) ÷ Cost, with benefits from wage/employment and productivity data vs control groups, tracked to year 3 (Card, Kluve & Weber).
What happens after the course?
Demonstrate → Apply → Recognise → Move; outcome recorded at 6 and 12 months.
How often are competencies refreshed?
Every 24 months at L2+, sooner if skill relevance falls below 80% (proposed).
What prevents AI misinformation entering training?
Expert verification before release, grounded tutors, human high-stakes assessment.
How do you ensure responsible AI?
Responsible AI is one of three graded dimensions at every level; bias audits; DPDP consent; human override. Evidence: Dell'Acqua — 19 pp worse outside AI's frontier.
How do you ensure inclusion?
Disadvantage-weighted payments, credit top-ups, vernacular/voice, assisted access; targets measured at conversion (women ≥45%, Tier-2/3 ≥70%).
How do you scale without compromising quality?
Six gates; independent evaluation; accreditation; Trainer Corps audit-and-renew cycle.
What single KPI decides success?
VACR — verified AI workforce conversion rate; pilot target ≥40%.
